taurajo_centaur_wind.description: Scout Ashhoof has watched the Kolkar raiding parties grow bolder along the eastern approach to Camp Taurajo. They strike the road near Far Watch Post, hit fast, and scatter before a proper warband can answer. She has buried two scouts this month and would like not to bury a third.
taurajo_centaur_wind.accept_text: Eight of them, out past Far Watch Post. They ride in small bands, hit a wagon or a scout, and vanish before we can pin them down. Thin their numbers. Maybe they'll think twice before the next raid. If you hear hooves behind you, do not turn around. Fight.
taurajo_centaur_wind.turn_in_text: Eight down. Good. The road is quieter already, though I doubt it will stay that way. Kolkar do not give up territory easily. Have some water. You have the look of someone who has been riding the dust.

taurajo_scout_outposts.description: With the raiders thinned near Far Watch Post, Ashhoof wants eyes on the outpost itself. Camp Taurajo needs to know whether the post is still standing, and still Horde. A watch post that falls silent is a watch post that has fallen, and nobody tells you until the centaur are at your gate.
taurajo_scout_outposts.accept_text: Far Watch Post sits east, right where the road bends toward Durotar. Walk it yourself. I want to know it is still standing, still ours. Speak to Outrider Kelsara if she's about. She'll tell you more than the reports do.
taurajo_scout_outposts.turn_in_text: Still standing. Good. Outrider Kelsara is holding that post with fewer grunts than I would like, but she is holding it. That is more than most can say. Thank you. I will sleep a little easier tonight.

taurajo_outriders_warning.description: Word from Far Watch Post is grim. The Kolkar are not just raiding any more, they are massing near Mor'shan Base Camp. Ashhoof wants that buildup broken before it turns into a real assault on the checkpoint. She says an army is only an army once it has a name, and this one has not chosen its yet.
taurajo_outriders_warning.accept_text: Mor'shan Base Camp is seeing more Kolkar than usual, and not just raiders. Marauders too, which means they are serious. Break it up before it becomes a siege. Nine of the raiders ought to do it. Bring your own water.
taurajo_outriders_warning.turn_in_text: That is a real dent in their numbers. Warsong Outrider Dask owes you a drink, if orcs drank anything but blackrock ale. Come and find him when the dust settles. He will pretend not to remember the debt.

taurajo_salvage_wagons.description: Grainkeeper Yura has lost more than one supply wagon to Kolkar raiders along the eastern road. She does not expect the wagons back, but the grain sacks the centaur scatter when they raid are still good, if someone is willing to collect them. Waste, to her, is the greater sin.
taurajo_salvage_wagons.accept_text: Kolkar don't eat grain, far as I know. They just scatter it when they hit a wagon, out of spite more than anything. Six sacks, wherever you find them, and the camp eats a little better this week. Don't take the ones that are torn. The rats have had those.
taurajo_salvage_wagons.turn_in_text: Six sacks. Dirty, but the grain is fine underneath. The camp thanks you, even if the wagons don't. I will bake tonight. If you smell bread, follow your nose, and bring a spoon.

taurajo_carvers_materials.description: Carver Ahonen works centaur horn into totems when he can get it, though he will not say why he prefers it to plain wood. Kolkar Marauders carry sun-bleached horns worth collecting, if the Marauders can be convinced to part with them. He suspects they can.
taurajo_carvers_materials.accept_text: Kolkar Marauders, not the Raiders. Their horns are worth something, carved right. Five, and do not ask me what I am making. You will see it eventually. Handle them with a cloth. The oil in your hands spoils the grain.
taurajo_carvers_materials.turn_in_text: Good horn. Clean break, no cracks. This will carve into something worth having. Come back when the season turns, and I will show you what it became. It will be better than you imagine. It always is.

taurajo_old_grudges.description: Elder Longtread remembers a Barrens before the Kolkar pressed this far east. He is willing to talk about it, if someone is willing to listen. He says the Kolkar have a reason for hating the Horde, and that every war is a story before it is a battle.
taurajo_old_grudges.accept_text: Sit a while. You are fighting the Kolkar out there. You might as well know why they fight us back. I will tell it plainly. It is not a kind story, and I am not a kind storyteller.
taurajo_old_grudges.turn_in_text: Now you understand it is not just territory. It is memory, on both sides. That is worth carrying with you. A fighter who knows why is slower to kill and quicker to end it. Go well.

taurajo_windhoofs_ledger.description: Hela Windhoof keeps Camp Taurajo's supply ledger, and the losses from Kolkar raids are piling up faster than she can write them off. She wants the raiding parties dealt with directly: enough to make a real dent, not just a token thinning. Her ink is running out.
taurajo_windhoofs_ledger.accept_text: Twelve. I know that is a lot to ask, but the ledger does not lie. We are losing more to raids than the camp can absorb. Whichever Kolkar you find, Raider, Marauder or Drudge, it all counts against the same problem. I will mark each one off.
taurajo_windhoofs_ledger.turn_in_text: Twelve down. The ledger breathes a little easier, and so do I. Thank you for this. I will write you in the margin, which is the highest honour I can give. Do not let it go to your head.

ratchet_trouble_coast.description: Customs Officer Prynn has heard reports of pirate activity along Merchant Coast, north of Ratchet's usual patrol routes. She wants confirmation before she takes it to Gazlowe. Gazlowe does not enjoy rumours. He enjoys evidence, with a signed receipt.
ratchet_trouble_coast.accept_text: Merchant Coast, north of here. Sailors are talking about pirate sails again. I need someone to actually go and look before I file a report that turns out to be fishermen's gossip. Look for flags, cannons, and the smell of cheap rum.
ratchet_trouble_coast.turn_in_text: So it is real. Southsea colours, you said? Gazlowe is not going to like hearing that. I will write it up properly and send it by the fastest runner. Thank you. You have saved me from a lot of paperwork.

ratchet_cutting_supply_lines.description: With pirate presence confirmed on Merchant Coast, Prynn wants their numbers cut down before they set up a permanent camp and start raiding Ratchet's shipping in earnest. Piracy is a business, she says, and every business starts with a small, polite beginning.
ratchet_cutting_supply_lines.accept_text: Eight Brigands, and do not be gentle about it. Every one you drop is one less problem for Ratchet's trade. They keep their coin in the left boot. I'm told. I've never checked.
ratchet_cutting_supply_lines.turn_in_text: That will slow them down. It will not stop them, but it will slow them down, and right now I will take it. Have this. And if you meet a pirate who wants to talk, tell him I'm busy.

ratchet_silence_guns.description: Fuzzek Boomwick does not like competition, and the Southsea Cannoneers dug in on Merchant Coast are exactly that: amateur artillery aimed at Ratchet's harbour. He wants them gone, partly for Ratchet's sake and partly out of professional pride. He has opinions about their fuse-work.
ratchet_silence_guns.accept_text: Cannoneers, on the coast. Their aim is terrible but their powder is real, and I do not like anyone playing with explosives who is not me. Six of them, gone. Stay low when they fire. The splash is the least of your worries.
ratchet_silence_guns.turn_in_text: Six fewer amateurs with gunpowder. The harbour is safer, and so is my professional reputation. Here, a little something. It is a fuse. Do not light it indoors. Do not light it near me.

ratchet_recovered_cargo.description: The Fence deals in things that fell off a ship, no questions asked, and the Southsea Brigands on Merchant Coast are sitting on strongboxes worth recovering, if someone is willing to take them by force. The Fence calls it "reclamation." The Brigands call it something else.
ratchet_recovered_cargo.accept_text: Strongboxes, off the Brigands on the coast. I do not care how you get them off their bodies. Just bring me five, still locked. If one is open, don't look inside. I mean it. Inside is a conversation neither of us wants.
ratchet_recovered_cargo.turn_in_text: Still locked, just how I like them. Do not ask what is inside. You would not get a cut anyway. Here is your fee. It is fair. I'm known for being fair, mostly when it costs me nothing.

ratchet_loose_lips.description: Smuggler Fintan hears things he probably should not, and lately what he is hearing about the Southsea Freebooters' plans is making him nervous enough to actually share it. He does not trust the walls. He has asked you to stand where the crates will muffle the sound.
ratchet_loose_lips.accept_text: I hear things at the docks. Lately what I am hearing has me looking over my shoulder more than usual. Ask me what you want to know, quietly. If anybody comes in, we are discussing the price of rope.
ratchet_loose_lips.turn_in_text: That is everything I know, and now I am going to pretend I never said any of it. Good luck out there. If you find a ship with a black sail, do not wave. Wave and they wave back, and then it is a conversation.

ratchet_bounty_saltspray.description: Bounty Hunter Drask has taken a contract on Captain Saltspray, the Southsea officer holding The Maiden's Dagger on Merchant Coast. The bounty is real, and so is the danger. Saltspray did not get to captain by being careless, and he has already outlived two others who tried.
ratchet_bounty_saltspray.accept_text: Saltspray is the one holding that fort together. Take the head off the operation and the rest scatters. This will not be easy. The contract would not pay this well if it were. Watch his hands. He fights dirty, and the dirt is on purpose.
ratchet_bounty_saltspray.turn_in_text: Saltspray is done. I will collect my contract fee, you collect yours. Fair trade. Do not look so grim. It was a good job, and no one should spend a good job feeling bad about it.

ratchet_barnacle_bet.description: Barnacle Bill missed his ship again, and in typical Bill fashion he has turned it into a bet. He has wagered a drinking buddy that adventurers passing through can clear a few Southsea stragglers faster than he can finish his tankard. The tankard is large, and getting emptier by the minute.
ratchet_barnacle_bet.accept_text: Five pirates, any kind, before I finish this tankard. I have coin riding on it. Probably shouldn't have bet against someone who was not even standing here yet, but here we are. Hurry. I am a fast drinker.
ratchet_barnacle_bet.turn_in_text: You actually did it! I owe Grizzik a round now, but I owe you more. Here. And do not tell Grizzik I was nervous. A man has to have some dignity, even if he has bet it.

org_word_from_road.description: Scout Windrider's reports on the Gold Road have gone quiet longer than they should. Orgrimmar wants someone to walk the road itself and confirm it is still passable. A silent scout is either busy or buried, and the capital has learned to ask which.
org_word_from_road.accept_text: The Gold Road runs from Mor'shan Rampart down toward the Crossroads. My last few reports from caravan masters have been thin. Walk it. See what is slowing them down. Keep your hand near your weapon and your eyes on the ditches.
org_word_from_road.turn_in_text: Bandits, you say. That tracks. The road has held worse, but it needs clearing before it holds much more. Thank you. I will pass it up the chain. They will pretend they knew, which is how it works.

org_keep_road_clear.description: With bandit activity confirmed on the Gold Road, Windrider wants their numbers cut. Caravans need to move, and they cannot do that with highwaymen picking them off one wagon at a time. The road is the Horde's pulse, she says, and it is beating slower than it should.
org_keep_road_clear.accept_text: Eight bandits, wherever they are staging their ambushes along the road. The caravans need it clear, and clear means fewer bandits, not zero patience for them. Follow the wheel-ruts. They know where the wagons slow.
org_keep_road_clear.turn_in_text: Eight down. The road is breathing easier, and so is every caravan master who runs it. Take this. And do not take it as a bribe. It is just that I like you better than the last one.

org_escalation.description: The bandits on the Gold Road are not just highwaymen any more. Windrider's reports now mention organised Cutthroats and mounted Outriders, which means someone is running this operation with real coordination. She does not like the idea of a mind behind the madness.
org_escalation.accept_text: This is not random banditry any more. Cutthroats and Outriders do not organise themselves. Break up whatever this is before it gets worse. Nine cutthroats ought to give us a name. Check their pockets for letters.
org_escalation.turn_in_text: Nine down, and no sign of who is running them, yet. That is a problem for another day. Today, the road is clear. I will have a runner take the letters to Orgrimmar. They will want a word with the author.

org_feathers_fury.description: Rethok the Hunter collects harpy feathers for reasons he does not fully explain, but he pays well, and the Witchwing Harpies in the Dry Hills have plenty to spare. He says feathers hold the shape of the thing that grew them. He says many things.
org_feathers_fury.accept_text: Witchwing Harpies, out in the Dry Hills. Nasty things, but their feathers are worth something to the right buyer. Six, and do not ask who the buyer is. Keep them dry. A wet feather forgets what it was.
org_feathers_fury.turn_in_text: Good feathers. Still humming with a little magic. Exactly what I needed. Take your pay, and an extra coin for not asking. I like the ones who don't ask. They live longer.

org_slayers_ring.description: The Witchwing Slayers are no ordinary harpies. They are Serena Bloodfeather's lieutenants, marked by the rings they carry, and Rethok wants them dealt with before going after Serena herself. A queen without her guard, he says, is a sorrow waiting to happen.
org_slayers_ring.accept_text: The Slayers lead the underlings in the Dry Hills. You can tell them by the rings they carry. Four of them, and Serena loses her chain of command. They fight in pairs. Do not let them take your flanks.
org_slayers_ring.turn_in_text: Four rings, four Slayers. Serena is down to just herself now. That is exactly where I want her. Rest your arms. The next fight will not be fair, and I want you to arrive on your own two feet.

org_serenas_head.description: With her lieutenants dead, Serena Bloodfeather stands alone in the Dry Hills, still attacking Horde caravans out of grief and revenge for her sister's death at Rexxar's hands. Rethok wants it ended, cleanly and for good, and without a trophy.
org_serenas_head.accept_text: Serena is alone now. She will not stop. Grief does not stop just because the people who might have spared you the fight are all dead. End it. She deserves better than to keep bleeding for a sister who is not coming back, and the caravans deserve to stop paying for it.
org_serenas_head.turn_in_text: It is done. I will not pretend that is a clean kind of victory. But the road is safer, and sometimes that has to be enough. Go home. Eat. Sleep. The hills will remember her, and so will I.

nb_toll_collectors.description: The Gold Road is the only honest thing in the Northern Barrens, and someone has started charging for it. Road Bandits wait at the bends, polite for exactly one sentence, and every wagon that cannot pay gets lighter. Hargak runs the waystation and has run out of patience.
nb_toll_collectors.accept_text: They wear their coats the wrong way round so you cannot tell who they are. I can tell. Thin them out along the bends and bring me what you find. Eight of them. If one tries to hand you a receipt, burn it. The receipt is the trap.
nb_toll_collectors.turn_in_text: Fewer coats, more wagons. That is the arithmetic I like. Here, the waystation's thanks. And if the bandits send a letter of complaint, you may deliver the reply yourself. It will be short.

nb_the_highwaymans_ledger.description: Bandits keep books. Hargak finds this both funny and useful. Every Road Bandit carries a stained page of who paid, who didn't, and which wagons are worth the trouble. Collect enough pages and you can read the route they plan next.
nb_the_highwaymans_ledger.accept_text: Five pages should do. Look in their coat linings. They think nobody checks there. Do not read them in the road. Wait until you are somewhere dull and quiet. Dull is safer.
nb_the_highwaymans_ledger.turn_in_text: Mm. They are going to hit the coast road next. I had better tell someone with a spear. Take this. I will send a rider before sundown. You have saved a wagon or three. They'll never know it was you.

nb_cutthroats_on_the_road.description: The pages named a crew: cutthroats on foot, outriders on beasts, working the stretch of road between the oasis fork and the coast. They are not toll collectors. They do not ask first. Hargak has seen what they leave behind, and he does not describe it.
nb_cutthroats_on_the_road.accept_text: Cutthroats move in pairs and outriders cover them from a distance. Take the outriders' bows first if you can. They hurt more than they look. Six cutthroats, five outriders. Keep to the ditch. It hides you better than the road.
nb_cutthroats_on_the_road.turn_in_text: The road is quiet. That is the first time in a season. You have earned more than I can pay, but this is what I have. Come back when the Gold Road needs a friend. It usually does.

nb_wreckers_beach.description: The Merchant Coast is the Barrens' loading dock, which is why every crab in the bay has decided it owns the pier. Tide-Wreckers pry the planks off cargo crates, drag them out to sea, and nobody sees either again. Kizzle has asked nicely. She is now asking differently.
nb_wreckers_beach.accept_text: Big, red, sulky. They hide in the surf. Crack a few and the rest will remember they have other places to be. Eight of them. Wear boots. The tide is cold and the crabs do not respect sandals.
nb_wreckers_beach.turn_in_text: Listen to that. Nothing! Not one claw! Take this, with the beachmaster's gratitude. I will tell the dockhands to leave a crate out for you tonight. Not one of the good ones. But close.

nb_salvage_rights.description: Southsea Brigands have been dragging cargo crates up the beach and prying them open. Anything they have not opened yet is, strictly speaking, still the Merchants'. Kizzle's definition of "strictly speaking" is flexible, and varies with the weather.
nb_salvage_rights.accept_text: Five crates. Do not open them. I know what is in them. Do not ask how. Bring them to me and I'll hand you a receipt. It will not be a good receipt, but it will be a receipt.
nb_salvage_rights.turn_in_text: These are mine! Er, the Merchants'. Same thing, really. Take this for your trouble. And if anyone asks, you found them washed up on the shore, and you left them with the first honest goblin you met.

nb_silence_the_cannons.description: The Southsea crews have mounted three cannons on the cliffs and are using them for target practice on anything that floats. Kizzle has a Ratchet-built guarantee that her pier is "definitely not in range." It definitely is, and the pilings are beginning to wince.
nb_silence_the_cannons.accept_text: Cannoneers stand behind the brigands. Cut through the brigands. Do not stand in a line. Six and six. If you hear a whistle overhead, throw yourself flat. The whistle is the polite part.
nb_silence_the_cannons.turn_in_text: Quiet again! Well, "quiet" for a harbour. Here, take this. It is cleaner than it looks. I'll put a notice on the pier that the cliffs are now officially unarmed. It's a lie, but it's a comforting one.

nb_captain_saltspray.description: Captain Saltspray runs the Southsea crew. He is not very good at it, but he is very loud, and the loud ones make the cannoneers brave. Take him down and the harbour might finally get some peace. Kizzle suspects the peace will last about a week.
nb_captain_saltspray.accept_text: He shows himself when his crew is winning. Make them stop winning. Then make him regret showing himself. Six brigands will stand between you and him. Pay no attention to his songs. He sings out of tune on purpose.
nb_captain_saltspray.turn_in_text: The captain is down, and the beach is ours again. Come back in a week. There will be a drink with your name on it. It will be a bad drink, but it will be a free one, and in Ratchet that counts for something.

nb_hounds_of_the_oasis.description: The Stagnant Oasis has not been fit to drink from in years, but it still draws every wanderer on the plains. Lately it also draws dervish hounds: lean, mange-ridden things that Kolkar dervishes breed and set loose. Mahri wants them gone before they learn what a campfire is for.
nb_hounds_of_the_oasis.accept_text: They circle first and bite after. Keep your back to something solid: a cliff, a tent, anything. Eight of them. If one of them sits and watches you, do not trust the quiet. That is the pack deciding.
nb_hounds_of_the_oasis.turn_in_text: They have stopped howling. I never realised how much of the night they filled. Take this. Sit by my fire a moment. A tauren should never go on without a rest and a story.

nb_curved_blades.description: Kolkar dervishes fight with curved blades they sharpen on the same stones they pray at. Mahri's scouts want half a dozen, not to use, but to read. The edges carry marks that say who trained whom, and where the dervishes learned their steps.
nb_curved_blades.accept_text: Cut them off the bodies. Bring me six and I will show you what the marks mean. Keep them wrapped. The edges are sharp enough to hurt through leather.
nb_curved_blades.turn_in_text: These are from the same forge. There is a smith feeding the whole camp. That is worth knowing. Take this. I will draw a map tonight. A smith has to eat, which means a smith has to be found.

nb_stormcallers.description: A band of Kolkar Stormcallers has taken up at the far side of the oasis, drawing lightning out of a sky that has not seen rain in months. It is not working. It is still giving everyone a headache. Mahri would like to be able to think again.
nb_stormcallers.accept_text: They stay together in the middle and the dervishes ring them. Break the ring, then the casters. Do not stand in the lightning. I mean that literally. Five of them. The sixth is a decoy, and the seventh is a mirage.
nb_stormcallers.turn_in_text: The sky is quiet. Wonderful. I can even hear the wind. Take this, with the camp's thanks. I'll make tea. It is a poor thing, and bitter, but it is warm, and tonight that is a miracle.

nb_verog_the_dervish.description: Verog leads the dervishes. He is fast, he is patient, and he is quick to be offended, which makes him the best bait the Kolkar could have used and the worst enemy anyone could have. The oasis will never be safe while he spins at the heart of it.
nb_verog_the_dervish.accept_text: He spins when he is angry, and he is always angry. Wait for the spin to wind down, then hit him. Dervishes around him first, though. You want him alone. Six of them. Do not look at the blades. Look at the feet.
nb_verog_the_dervish.turn_in_text: Verog is dead. I never thought I would see it. Take this, and let me be the first to buy you a drink. I will tell the camp you earned it. They will not believe me. That is how you know it is true.

nb_raiders_at_the_gate.description: Far Watch Post holds the eastern road, and the Kolkar know it. Every dawn another band of raiders rides up the headland, circles the watchtower and tests the palisade. Kelsara has counted forty since the last full moon. She has stopped counting them as people.
nb_raiders_at_the_gate.accept_text: They test the weak spots. There aren't any. Convince them of that with a spear. Eight of them. If one carries a white flag, do not trust it. The white flag is the rudest trick.
nb_raiders_at_the_gate.turn_in_text: Nothing at the palisade for an hour now. Almost suspicious. Take this and do not question luck. Luck is a river. It does not like to be asked where it is going.

nb_war_pennants.description: Every Kolkar warband carries a pennant, a strip of dyed hide on a stick that tells the others who is in charge. Take enough of them and the bands lose their way. Kelsara is tired of reading the same colours at the same hour every morning.
nb_war_pennants.accept_text: Six pennants. Do not burn them. I want to read them first. The colours tell me who is riding with whom, and I would very much like to know who has made friends.
nb_war_pennants.turn_in_text: The colours match three different bands. They have united. That is bad. Take this, and be quick going back out. The three of them will not stay united for long. They never do. But long enough to be trouble.

nb_scoutriders_on_the_headland.description: Kolkar Scoutriders ride the headland every night, measuring the watchtower's blind spots. Kelsara has no blind spots. She does have a lot of drudges stealing from the supply line while the scouts watch. She would like both problems gone, in that order or any other.
nb_scoutriders_on_the_headland.accept_text: Scoutriders on beasts, drudges on foot. Cut the drudges down first. They are slow, and the scouts will come to rescue them. Six and six. Do not follow the scouts off the headland. It is not worth the climb.
nb_scoutriders_on_the_headland.turn_in_text: The headland is quiet again. You earned this, and a place in my orders. I will mention your name when I report to the Warchief's people. Do not tell anyone. It will go to your head.

nb_kragg_the_wall_breaker.description: Kragg is a warbrand chief who has never met a palisade he could not test. He rides a hide-clad warbeast and brings a ram. Far Watch's wall has stood for ten years, and he has decided that is too long.
nb_kragg_the_wall_breaker.accept_text: He comes at dusk, usually. Warbrands first, then him. If he reaches the wall, we all know what happens. Six of them. Do not try to stop the ram. Stop the man pulling it.
nb_kragg_the_wall_breaker.turn_in_text: Kragg is down. The wall holds. I will raise a drink and a banner. Take this, the Post's thanks. And if you see a ram lying in the grass, give it a kick for me. It has earned it.

nb_slugs_in_the_reeds.description: The Slug Fens used to be only slow, wet and quiet. Then the slugs got big. Dugmok's wardens keep the causeway open, but the slugs are creeping across it at night, and nobody wants to explain why a caravan went in and the cargo came out as soup.
nb_slugs_in_the_reeds.accept_text: Pale, fat, and bigger than a dog. Cut them back from the causeway. If they wriggle, hit harder. Eight of them. Keep your boots on. The mud is the least of the fen's problems.
nb_slugs_in_the_reeds.turn_in_text: Quiet. Thick, wet, honest quiet. Thank you. Take this, with the fen's thanks. I'll tell the wardens the causeway is clear. They will not believe me, and then they will see it themselves.

nb_venom_glands.description: Fen slugs carry venom glands in their backs, a green sac that makes a first-rate poison if you know how to cure it. Dugmok knows how. He would rather not touch them himself, and has said so in several languages, none of them polite.
nb_venom_glands.accept_text: Cut them out whole. Do not pop them. If you do, we will be burying a tauren. Six, whole, wrapped in a wet cloth. A dry cloth makes them brittle.
nb_venom_glands.turn_in_text: Good clean glands. I will make something for the next caravan. Take this. And wash your hands in the stream, not the fen. The fen takes what you leave it, and what it leaves you, you do not want.

nb_peat_hearts.description: Deep in the fens the peat has started to move. Peat Shamblers, mud and root and old bog-oak, shuffle along the causeway at night. At the heart of each is a warm core that Dugmok can burn through a cold winter, if he can get it out.
nb_peat_hearts.accept_text: You will have to break them. Hit the middle. The heart is a lump the size of your fist. Six shamblers, five hearts. If a heart goes cold in your hands, drop it. It has forgotten what it was.
nb_peat_hearts.turn_in_text: Ha! Warm already. You are a wonder. Take this. I will keep a fire lit in your honour. The smoke is thick, but the heat is real, and it will last until spring.

nb_old_mire_maw.description: Something old and very hungry lives at the bottom of the deep fen: Old Mire-Maw, a crocolisk older than the causeway and wider than a wagon. Dugmok has lost three wardens to it. He has decided that is enough.
nb_old_mire_maw.accept_text: It hides in the deep pools, at the end of the causeway. Do not stand in the water. Do not stand near the water. If you can, do not stand. Five crocolisks first, to wake it properly. Then let it come to you.
nb_old_mire_maw.turn_in_text: Mire-Maw is dead. I never thought I would say it. Come back and I will carve you something from its tooth. A warden's gift is a small one, but it comes from a grateful heart.

nb_rig_crews.description: Nix used to work for the Venture Company, before he learned what they were doing in the fen. Now he watches the rig from a rusted shack and counts the crews. They have been drilling day and night, and the ground is bleeding black. He wants the crews gone, preferably without anyone he likes in the way.
nb_rig_crews.accept_text: The drillers are the loud ones. Stop the noise and the guards come out. They are quieter, and nastier. Eight drillers. Do not light a match. Do not light anything. The air is thicker than it smells.
nb_rig_crews.turn_in_text: Quiet! Real quiet. The fen has a pulse again. Take this, from a man who knows what it is worth. I'll have a drink waiting when you come by. It won't be good. It'll be mine.

nb_pressure_gauges.description: Every rig has a gauge, and every gauge tells a story: how hard they are drilling, how deep, and how close the whole fen is to blowing. Nix wants five of them from the pumpjack guards. He has lost the nerve to ask nicely, and has found a new nerve for asking less nicely.
nb_pressure_gauges.accept_text: Pumpjack guards keep them on a chain. Cut the chain. Do not cut the guard's friends. They fight back. Five guards, five gauges. If a needle is in the red, do not tap it. Walk away.
nb_pressure_gauges.turn_in_text: Ha. Look at that needle. They are drilling too deep. It is going to blow. Take this and keep your distance. I will write to the Company, and they will ignore the letter, and I'll write again.

nb_sludge_samples.description: Where the oil has pooled, the sludge has started to move. Sludge Elementals, black, sticky, and very angry. Nix wants samples to prove to the Company that its drilling is doing this. He would also like not to be near them while they are collected.
nb_sludge_samples.accept_text: Take the samples from the middle. They leave a slick. Careful. The goop does not come off. Six samples, six elementals. Wear something you will not miss. You will not get it back.
nb_sludge_samples.turn_in_text: Look at that. Pure, black, and very illegal. They will not be able to deny it. Take this. I will wash the jars in the stream tomorrow. The stream will not forgive me, but the Company will.

nb_supervisor_lugwizzle.description: Lugwizzle runs the rig. He screams a lot, throws wrenches, and signs every order. If he stops, the rig stops. If the rig stops, the fen heals. Nix has drawn you a map to the pumphouse.
nb_supervisor_lugwizzle.accept_text: He is usually in the pumphouse, shouting. He throws oil. Do not stand in it. Six drillers will be underfoot. They are loyal because they are afraid, and afraid people do not stop when you ask.
nb_supervisor_lugwizzle.turn_in_text: Lugwizzle is down, and the rig is quiet. Take this. I owe you more than I will ever have. I'll dig a hole for his wrench and put a flower on it. Not because he deserves it. Because I do.

nb_engineer_whirleygig.description: With Lugwizzle gone, the engineer is panicking. Whirleygig is the one who actually made the drillers work, and he is building something large and noisy in the back of the shop. Nix says it is going to explode. Nix says a lot of things, but he is usually right about that one.
nb_engineer_whirleygig.accept_text: He has turrets. Kill the guards, then him. Do not be near him when he trips the switch. Five guards. If the room begins to hum, run. Do not stop to look at what is humming.
nb_engineer_whirleygig.turn_in_text: The thing is dead, the engineer is dead, and the fen will heal in time. Take this. It is the last of what I own that is worth giving. I will keep the shack for a while. Somebody has to keep an eye on the pipes.

nb_claim_jumpers.description: The Boulder Lode was a Horde claim before the Venture Company moved in. Now Miners swing picks on its walls and Overseers shout in its tunnels, and Gruda has the paperwork to prove who owns the ore. The paperwork is not helping.
nb_claim_jumpers.accept_text: Go in and clear the miners from the lower galleries. They are not soldiers. They will still hit you with a pick. Eight of them. Watch the ceiling. The Company has not shored it up properly in a decade.
nb_claim_jumpers.turn_in_text: The lower galleries are ours again. I can hear the dust settling. Take this. I'll hang a sign at the entrance: "Horde claim." Underneath, in small letters: "Mind the ceiling."

nb_heart_of_the_vein.description: The Elementals in the mine are made of the same rock as the walls, and the walls are laced with crystal. If Gruda can read the vein, she can tell how much the Company has already taken. Sample cores from the big ones, and bring them out in one piece.
nb_heart_of_the_vein.accept_text: Break them open. You will find a glowing core in each. Bring me five. I will read the vein. Do not drop them. They are warm, and the warmth is not a comfort.
nb_heart_of_the_vein.turn_in_text: The vein is rich. Richer than they let on. And they have taken nearly half. Take this, with my thanks. I'll take the cores to the guild and have them swear to it. Evidence is a heavy thing to carry. Thank you for carrying it.

nb_sprites_in_the_seams.description: The ore sprites are small, bright and mean. They live in the crystal seams and bite anything that gets close. Gruda wants their shards, a chip off each, for her assay table. She says the sprites are the vein's way of talking, and she would like to hear what it has to say.
nb_sprites_in_the_seams.accept_text: Quick and glowing. Hit them while they are pausing to sparkle. Do not breathe their dust. Six sprites, six shards. If one begins to sing, put your fingers in your ears.
nb_sprites_in_the_seams.turn_in_text: Beautiful. And they test out rich, too. Take this, with the claim's thanks. I'll write up the report tonight. The Company will say the sprites are a myth. The sprites will be offended.

nb_prospector_delvik.description: Delvik was Gruda's partner once. He sold the claim's map to the Venture Company for a promise and a bag of silver, and now hides in a side adit with a rifle and a bad conscience. Gruda would like him to explain himself, if possible. If not, it will not be a surprise.
nb_prospector_delvik.accept_text: He is in a side adit off the middle gallery, behind a pile of rubble. He shoots first. Tinkerers will keep him company. Clear them out and you have done most of it. Five tinkerers. If he speaks, do not answer. He argues better than he shoots.
nb_prospector_delvik.turn_in_text: So he did get what he deserved. I would wish it a quieter end, but I am not sorry. Take this. I'll bury the map where it belongs, in the back of a drawer, with the other mistakes.

nb_foreman_grills.description: At the top of the mine, round a vein of blue crystal, Foreman Grills runs the Company's crew. He wears an iron hat, shouts orders through a bullhorn and is, in his own estimation, the cleverest man ever to hold a pick. Gruda says he is only the loudest.
nb_foreman_grills.accept_text: He is at the top, in the crystal chamber. Overseers guard the way up. Take them out and he is alone, if you can call a man with a bullhorn alone. Four overseers. Bring earplugs. The bullhorn is louder than it has a right to be.
nb_foreman_grills.turn_in_text: Grills is dead, the claim is ours, and the vein will outlast us all. Take this, with the claim's honour. I'll have the bullhorn mounted over the entrance, as a warning. Or a joke. I haven't decided.

nb_siege_lines.description: Mor'shan Base Camp sits under the Rampart like a thorn in the Kaldorei's side. Kolkar Warbrands surround it. Dask does not blame them. He would attack, too. He would like the Warbrands to stop camping on the supply road.
nb_siege_lines.accept_text: Warbrands are tough, loud and always in a group of four. Break one group and the rest will think twice. Do not think twice yourself. Six of them. Bring a shield, and a reason to fight.
nb_siege_lines.turn_in_text: The supply road is clear! Well, clearer. Take this, from a grateful outrider. I'll tell my captain it was you. He will say "who?" and I will say "the one with the sword," and he'll nod.

nb_break_the_scouts.description: Scoutriders ride the hills above the Base Camp and report every movement to the Rampart. Dask does not mind being watched. He minds being shot at, which the scouts do for sport.
nb_break_the_scouts.accept_text: They shoot from range and run. Chase the slow ones. The fast ones will come back. Eight of them. If one stops to taunt you, kill him. That is the one that matters.
nb_break_the_scouts.turn_in_text: They have stopped watching. Good. I can have a quiet breakfast. Take this. I have not had a quiet breakfast since spring, and I did not know how much I missed it.

nb_scout_captain_vrek.description: Vrek commands the Rampart-watchers and is the one who tells the Kaldorei when to shoot. He rides a swift, sharp-eyed hawk and sees everything on the plain. Dask wants him blinded, preferably permanently.
nb_scout_captain_vrek.accept_text: He hides among the scoutriders. If you can get to him, he is weak. If he gets to you, you are not. Six raiders will try to stop you. Do not let them. Do not stand where the hawk can see you.
nb_scout_captain_vrek.turn_in_text: Vrek is down. The Rampart cannot see us for a day or two. That may be all we need. Take this. I'll mark the day on the map. It is not a victory. It is an opening.

nb_pickets_past_the_wall.description: The Rampart is the Horde's wall against the Kaldorei, and it is a wall with a very thin side. Sentinel Pickets and Archers hold the strip just north of it, firing at anyone who gets near the gate. Korvash wants the strip cleared. He is tired of being polite.
nb_pickets_past_the_wall.accept_text: The pickets hold the line. The archers cover them from the cliffs. Take the archers first if you can. Do not be proud. Six pickets, four archers. Keep your head down. Their aim is not a compliment.
nb_pickets_past_the_wall.turn_in_text: The strip is quiet. For now. They will send more. They always do. Take this. I will tell the garrison it was a good fight. It was not. But it was a necessary one.

nb_signal_horns.description: Every Sentinel Picket carries a signal horn: one blast and the whole forest answers. Korvash wants them silenced before the Kaldorei figure out how thin the Rampart really is. He is not proud of the thinness, and he does not intend to advertise it.
nb_signal_horns.accept_text: Cut them off their belts. Quick, before they sound them. Bring me five. If a horn sounds, run. Do not try to be brave. Brave is slower than fast.
nb_signal_horns.turn_in_text: Five horns. Five fewer calls for help. That is a good day. Take this. I will hang them in the barracks as a warning. Or a decoration. The recruits are not particular.

nb_moonspeakers.description: Behind the pickets stand Moonspeakers, night elf priestesses who call down light on anyone who falls. They are the reason the pickets keep coming back. Take them out and the line breaks. Korvash admires their courage, and intends to end it.
nb_moonspeakers.accept_text: They stay in the back, glowing. Close on them quickly. They run if you wait. Five of them. Do not look at the light. It is meant to blind. It does.
nb_moonspeakers.turn_in_text: The line is breaking. That is what we have been waiting for. Take this, with the Rampart's thanks. I'll light a candle for them, tonight, in my own way. They were brave. They were also wrong.

nb_warden_ilthae.description: The Sentinels' commander at the wall is Warden Ilthae, an old, steady, silver-haired woman who has not lost a skirmish in twenty years. Korvash respects her. He would still like her dead.
nb_warden_ilthae.accept_text: She has a glaive, a bad temper and no fear. Do not fight her in the open. Do not fight her at all, if you can avoid it. But you cannot. Six pickets guard her. She will watch you fall, and she will not blink.
nb_warden_ilthae.turn_in_text: Ilthae is dead. The strip is ours. Take this, and may the wall hold a little longer. I will not cheer. She earned better than a cheer, and so did you.

nb_feathers_on_the_wind.description: The Dry Hills belong to the Witchwings, harpies who have learned a few tricks from somewhere dark. Zan'ula tracks them for a living. She would like fewer of them to track, and more of the hills to walk in.
nb_feathers_on_the_wind.accept_text: They fly low over the ridges and strike from behind. Keep your back to a hill and you will be fine. Eight of them. If one calls your name, it is only the wind. Usually.
nb_feathers_on_the_wind.turn_in_text: Good. Quiet in the hills. For a day or so. Take this. I'll mark the ridge where you fought. Someone will want to know where the hunting was good.

nb_hexed_totems.description: The Witchwing Windcallers carve hex-totems and hang them in the high rocks. Zan'ula does not know what they do, only that she dreams badly near them. She would like them taken down, and the dreams with them.
nb_hexed_totems.accept_text: Pull the totems from the Windcallers. Do not look at them for long. Five totems, four Windcallers. If you dream of feathers tonight, tell me. It will mean you have kept one.
nb_hexed_totems.turn_in_text: Mm. They feel wrong, even in a bag. I will burn them. Thank you. Take this. If I seem distracted tonight, it is only that I am listening to the wind. It has changed its song.

nb_hillcrest_stalkers.description: Hillcrest Stalkers have been hunting the trail between the hills. They are patient, grey and cunning. Zan'ula wants pelts, and the hills quiet again. She says a good pelt keeps the winter out, and a bad one only keeps the story in.
nb_hillcrest_stalkers.accept_text: Stalkers wait on the high ledges. Look up before you walk under a ridge. Eight of them. If one yawns at you, do not be charmed. That is the signal.
nb_hillcrest_stalkers.turn_in_text: Good pelts. I will sell the rest at the Crossroads. Take this. And do not tell anyone how many you took. They will want more. Pelts, I mean. Stories are free.

nb_serena_bloodfeather.description: Serena Bloodfeather leads the Witchwings. She has an old blood-feud with the Horde and a long memory. Zan'ula has tracked her for years and never gotten close. You might. You will certainly try.
nb_serena_bloodfeather.accept_text: She flies in at the end of a long hunt. Slayers first, always. If Serena sees you, run to the nearest ridge and fight there. Five slayers. She will not be alone. She never is.
nb_serena_bloodfeather.turn_in_text: Serena is dead. The hills are quiet. I cannot believe it. Take this, with a hunter's thanks. I'll light a pipe for her tonight. She was a great enemy, and a worse friend, and a better queen than most.

nb_roost_raiders.description: Serena's Hollow is a cliff-gorge that winds up to a harpy roost, and the harpies who live there do not love visitors. Rohna is an earthcaller, a spirit-speaker, and she can feel the roost crying out. It is a bad cry. She wants it quieted.
nb_roost_raiders.accept_text: Go in through the cave mouth. Bonepickers hold the lower nests. They are small, mean, and love the taste of tauren. Six of them. Do not step on the eggs. They remember.
nb_roost_raiders.turn_in_text: Better. The earth is calmer. Take this, with the spirits' thanks. I will leave an offering at the mouth tonight. The spirits like honey. I like honey too, but they are more demanding.

nb_down_from_the_roost.description: The harpies line their nests with down. Fine, white, and warm. Rohna's totem-carvers use it in their rites. She would like six handfuls, and no more harpies in her sleep.
nb_down_from_the_roost.accept_text: Pull the down from the nests. Mind the sentries. They watch from the high ledges. Six handfuls, four sentries. Be quick. A harpy nest is a poor place to dawdle.
nb_down_from_the_roost.turn_in_text: Soft as a promise. Thank you. The spirits will be pleased. Take this. I will sew it into the totem-wraps and bless them. They will keep out the cold. And, I hope, the dreams.

nb_windcallers_perch.description: High in the gorge sits a perch where Windcaller Skreeva commands the winds that blow the harpies up and down the cliff. Rohna says the winds listen to her. She would rather they listened to someone else.
nb_windcallers_perch.accept_text: She stands on the east ledge, above the middle of the gorge. Her Windcallers keep the air thick. Take them first, then her. Four of them. Do not fight with the wind at your back. It will not stay there.
nb_windcallers_perch.turn_in_text: Skreeva is dead. The winds are quiet. I can hear them breathing. Take this. I will teach them a new song, if they are willing. They have been shouting for so long.

nb_harpy_matriarch.description: At the top of the gorge sits the roost, a great bowl of nests, and in the centre of it, the Matriarch, mother of every harpy in the hills. Rohna says her cry is the one the earth keeps answering. End it, and the hollow will be quiet.
nb_harpy_matriarch.accept_text: She will not leave the nest. She will call every harpy in the roost the moment she sees you. Do not fight her with the whole flock watching. Six harpies first. Take them one by one, quietly, and the Matriarch will have no choice but to come to you.
nb_harpy_matriarch.turn_in_text: The Matriarch is dead. The roost is silent, and the earth is quiet. I will sing the spirits home. Take this, and my thanks. When you hear the wind in the Hollow, know that it is thanking you in its own way.
